parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the need for an installable math_verify package with parse, verify, config exports, grader behavior, CLI, examples, and local tests.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent spawned direct children for latex API and upstream package inspection but also kept implementation ownership itself; both direct children performed overlapping investigation and implementation in the same workspace.
parallel.implementation: The parent downloaded upstream math-verify, inspected parser and grader APIs, wrote the package from scratch, added project scaffolding and tests, and ran local install, pytest, and smoke checks.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent delivered its own final package tree and did not integrate child-written project files or the child-upstream patched tree after interrupting the direct children.
parallel.verification: The parent compiled/imported the package, installed it editable, ran pytest with 10 passing local tests, ran CLI/smoke parse and verify checks, and noted no submit command was available locally.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Two direct children were interrupted while active, leaving their implementation/probing work abandoned; the official evaluator later found 5 of 192 tests still failing.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the empty workspace and the same need for parser, verifier, sympy_expr_eq, config classes, CLI entry points, docs, examples, tests, and broad edge-case support.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial agent kept all research, implementation, fixing, verification, packaging, and finalization in one local thread with no delegated child work.
serial.implementation: The serial agent probed latex2sympy behavior, wrote parser, grader, verifier, metric, tasks, CLI, docs, examples, and tests, then iterated through bugs in over-collection, prose parsing, timeout behavior, constants, console wrappers, and boxed answer handling.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial artifact was one coherent locally maintained tree with parser/grader/verifier files, CLI wrappers, docs, examples, and three test files.
serial.verification: The serial run repeatedly ran direct parse/verify checks, CLI checks, and pytest until 13 local tests passed, then finalized after checking the file tree and pyproject entry points.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite the longer local iteration, the official evaluator found 34 of 192 tests still failing, so the serial implementation remained substantially incomplete against hidden coverage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the installable project, parser/verifier API, pyproject, CLI, examples, tests, and special expression handling requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same project obligations and explicitly iterated over many prompt edge cases, including boxed answers, prose extraction, timeouts, constants, and CLI behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both runs targeted the same requirements; serial spent more single-thread time on edge-case refinement while parallel leaned more on upstream mirroring and still scored higher officially.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent spawned children for latex API and upstream inspection but retained enough implementation ownership to build and test its own package.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent used no child agents and owned research, implementation, testing, packaging, and closure itself.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had overlapping delegated work and parent implementation; serial had a single owner and no child lifecycle to reconcile.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child task payloads are encrypted in the raw logs, but observable activity shows children had the main prompt and investigated or implemented overlapping math-verify behavior; one nested child returned useful upstream findings.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial gathered runtime facts directly and used them immediately in local implementation and fixes without cross-agent handoff boundaries.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The key context difference was lifecycle rather than missing task facts: parallel had returned or partial child information around active children, while serial kept findings in the same thread.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent mirrored upstream behavior and wrote package files in two large patches, with local tests and examples focused around core parser/grader coverage.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote its own implementation and applied many incremental parser/CLI fixes after local checks exposed over-collection, prose parsing, timeout, constants, and boxed-answer issues.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's parent implementation was more upstream-shaped and achieved better hidden score; serial had more visible local refinement but still missed more hidden tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent waited, listed still-running direct children, and explicitly interrupted both before they finalized their own work or returned direct final results.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; local checks and fixes stayed in the same thread through final pytest and final answer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the main coordination difference: parallel abandoned active child work, while serial had no join/cancel step and carried its own work through closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote into the same workspace, but the delivered tree came from the parent after interrupting those children; no proven final overwrite or same-file reconciliation event is needed beyond the cancellation chain.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial integrated a single coherent final tree, checked file listings, and removed cache artifacts without cross-agent provenance ambiguity.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had shared-workspace side effects from children that became abandoned after interruption; serial's integration state was locally owned throughout.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran compile/import checks, editable install, pytest with 10 local tests passing, direct smoke checks, and CLI verification, then closed without a local submit command.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran repeated parse/verify checks, CLI checks, and pytest until 13 tests passed, then closed without a local submit command.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had a broader visible local test suite, but official hidden evaluation still failed more tests than parallel; local acceptance evidence did not predict the final score ordering.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel closed in about 608 agent seconds and interrupted two active children after the parent package and smoke tests were already in place.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used about 1051 agent seconds, kept iterating on local fixes until pytest passed, and then finalized after checking package entry points and file listings.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent budget on children it later cancelled and closed sooner; serial spent longer on one-thread iteration, but both official outcomes remained failures.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The completed official records make the pair a both_fail case: parallel passed 187 of 192 tests and serial passed 158 of 192. The solutions differ materially in score and process, but not in pass/fail outcome. The main parallel-specific adverse coordination event is explicit interruption of two active direct children after they had produced or modified implementation state, while the serial run kept the implementation and verification loop local. That event is adverse process evidence, not an explanation for a discordant official outcome.
parallel_contributors: Parent mirrored upstream package behavior and produced a high-scoring local implementation.
Two direct children were interrupted while still running after doing implementation or upstream-patch work.
serial_contributors: Serial iterated longer in one thread with 13 local tests passing.
Serial still missed more hidden cases than parallel, as shown by the official 158 of 192 score.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel's parent implementation was closer to upstream math-verify and scored 187/192.
Serial visibly fixed more local edge cases but delivered an implementation that scored 158/192.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no pass/fail outcome difference; retained label is adverse parallel process evidence only
